entities.summary: Muhammad ibn Mahmud al-Amuli (d. 1352) was a renowned Persian physician from Amol, Iran, who made significant contributions to the field of medicine, particularly in the areas of pharmacology and surgery. His work on the use of herbal remedies and surgical techniques was widely adopted during the Middle Ages. Al-Amuli's writings were also notable for their emphasis on the importance of observation, experimentation, and critical thinking in the pursuit of medical knowledge. As a key figure in the development of Persian medicine, al-Amuli played a crucial role in shaping the medical landscape of the Islamic world during the 14th century. His legacy extended beyond his own time, influencing the work of later physicians and scientists, including Ibn Sina and Avicenna, who would go on to make even more significant contributions to the field. One of al-Amuli's most enduring legacies is the continued use of herbal remedies in traditional medicine, a practice that remains popular to this day in many parts of the world.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Al-Amuli's work on pharmacology and surgery made significant contributions to the field of medicine, particularly in the Islamic world during the 14th century. His legacy extended beyond his own time, influencing later physicians and scientists, including Ibn Sina and Avicenna.
